Subject: Request: additional pilot credits for Helixium evaluation

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the initial credits to run our integration pilot — the team has started smoke-testing Redwood with our internal tooling. We hit a couple of unexpected blockers during the first week (tokenization mismatch on our preprocessor + transient auth errors from our side) which ate into the pilot credits faster than we anticipated.

Can we request an additional 50k free-eval tokens and a two-week extension to the pilot window? We believe another run will show the latency and cost benefits you demonstrated on the call. I attached a short usage export (helixium_usage_report.csv) and a screenshot of one of the integration errors.

We appreciate the help — happy to hop on a quick call if you want more context.

Best,
Rajiv Menon
Head of Integrations, Helixium
rajiv@helixium.com

Hi Rajiv — thanks for the note and the attachments (got them). Quick clarifying Qs before I escalate to our pilot credits team:

- Is this the same Helixium account that we extended last month? (I see a prior one-off extension in our notes.)
- Rough estimate: how many active devs are running the test (concurrent users) and what workload pattern (burst/steady)?

I want to be transparent — we have a few accounts that repeatedly request extra grants instead of upgrading to paid pilots. I don’t want that to block you, but I do need to run this through a short review. I’m looping in Ben from growth so he can surface any prior history.

I’ll follow up within 48 hours.

Thanks,

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: additional pilot credits for Helixium evaluation

Jordan / Monica — quick internal summary from our end after pulling account logs:

- Helixium (customer id: HLX-3342) was granted an initial 75k eval tokens on 2027-04-05.
- We approved a one-time 30k top-up on 2027-05-18 after they reported setup delays.
- Account shows three distinct API keys tied to the same billing email and three signups from proxied IP ranges in a ~36 hour window on 2027-05-16.
- Recent usage pattern: many short bursts of high token usage (possible scripted runs) rather than steady integration tests.

Attached a cleaned usage export — look for spikes in the `2027-06-02` to `2027-06-08` range. My read: borderline abuse pattern but also possible legitimate re-runs after fixes. Recommend we request more evidence before approving another top-up.

Proposed next steps:
- Ask Helixium for confirmation of number of test nodes and engineering contacts.
- Request a short repro video or a staging integration run window so we can observe traffic.
- If they provide satisfactory proof, approve a limited 20k token top-up and a 7-day extension; otherwise deny and offer a paid pilot seat with a small discount.

Ben Carter
Growth Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachment: helixium_usage_export-clean.csv (CSV, 8 KB)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: additional pilot credits for Helixium evaluation

Thanks Ben — I ran a quick check with the fraud signals team:

- High-risk indicators: multiple API keys for same billing email, proxied IP clusters, and unusually short-lived keys used during heavy token bursts.
- No clear evidence of credential compromise yet, but pattern matches other cases where customers were cycling trial grants.

I recommend a conservative approach: do not auto-grant a large top-up. Instead we should:

1) Ask Helixium to schedule a 30-minute staging run during which we can observe traffic and validate tokens (window: next 72 hours).
2) Offer a one-time 15k token extension conditional on that observation.
3) Flag the account in our backend (trial_escalation=true) so future automated grants require manual approval.

If they refuse or fail to provide a staging run, deny further free credits and propose the discounted paid pilot (20% off first month) as an alternative.

Monica Patel
Risk & Trust | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@helixium.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: additional pilot credits for Helixium evaluation

Hi Rajiv — thanks for the details and the export you sent earlier. Quick status update: we did an internal review and have a couple of asks before we can approve more free credits.

- Can you confirm the engineering contacts who will run the staging window and the number of test nodes?
- Please schedule a 30-minute staging run in the next 72 hours (we can provide a time slot and observe).

We want to be helpful: if you can run the staging and we observe expected integration traffic, we will approve a one-time 15,000 token top-up and extend the pilot by 7 days. If scheduling the staging is not possible, we cannot approve additional free credits at this time, but we can provide a paid pilot seat with a 20% discount on the first month to support a larger evaluation.

Appreciate the understanding — we’re trying to balance legitimate pilots and preventing repeated free-credit cycles. Let me know a few time windows and the best engineer to loop in.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
